guardrail: These decisions resolve only source gaps. They do not weaken the publisher-clear rule that after a Wizard opens a trick every later card is legal and no led suit arises.

clarifications.decision: Use exactly one ordinary card of every rank 1 through 13 in each of the four named suits, plus four Wizards and four Jesters. Magier and Zauberer denote the same Wizard type.
Player 0 is the first dealer and scorekeeper. At each non-final round boundary collect and reshuffle all 60 cards, then rotate the dealer one player clockwise and deal the next round.
When the revealed card is a Wizard, the dealer must choose exactly one of the four suits as trump after receiving and viewing their hand. Declining to choose is not legal.
Predictions are integers from zero through the current hand size, made clockwise beginning with the dealer's left neighbor. The base game imposes no restriction on the sum of predictions.

After one or more leading Jesters, the first subsequently played ordinary card establishes the led suit. If a Wizard is played before any ordinary card, the trick remains colorless, every later card remains legal, and the first Wizard wins.
Players tied for the highest final score are joint winners.
Each player observes their own cards and only opponents' hand sizes. Predictions, revealed trump, played cards, turn information, and scores are public.
